evidence.claim: The disputed charge is a $49.00 card-present purchase (ProductCD W) on 2016-12-10 13:01:21 in billing region 330.0, country 87, with a model risk score of 0.40. Being product W it carries no identity record, so no device or proxy evidence exists for it.

Billing region 330.0 is long established for this card, not novel: 42 prior transactions there before the disputed charge, the first on 2016-07-09, and 5 more in the same week (2016-12-07 x4, 2016-12-09). The card had 980 transactions before this one across 54 regions.

The amount is unremarkable for this card: 53 prior charges between $48.50 and $49.50, against a median transaction of $68.01 and a p95 of $425.66. The disputed charge is below the cardholder's median.
The channel and product are the cardholder's norm: 1,080 of 1,134 transactions on this card are in person, and 34 of the 42 prior transactions in region 330.0 are the same product code W.

Transaction 3530056, a $116.93 card-present purchase in the same region 330.0 49 minutes earlier at 12:12:41, scored 0.88 and is the highest-risk transaction on this card in the alert week. If the disputed charge is fraud, this is very likely part of the same episode.

This cardholder has reported unrecognized activity five times and been right every time: CC-2817, CC-2935, CC-3327, CC-3682 and CC-4957 were all closed as confirmed fraud on this same card. A denial from this customer carries an unusually strong track record.

The disputed charge does not match this card's own fraud signature. All four prior out_of_region_use cases involved card-present use in billing regions the card had no history in (126.0, 387.0, 158.0, 272.0) while the cardholder retained the card; region 330.0 has five months of history. The fifth case, CC-3327, was mixed-channel account takeover, which also does not fit a single in-person charge.

No shared-origin evidence. Billing region 330.0 shows 18 transactions scoring 0.70 or above out of 608 across 2016-12-08 to 2016-12-12, against 13 of 552 in the same five-day window a month earlier. That is no spike, and the 15 other cards involved show no common device or timing structure, so policy R6 and R9 do not apply.

The bank's own model is not alarmed: the disputed transaction scored 0.40, below the 0.70 band, while the adjacent 12:12:41 charge scored 0.88. The score is treated here as one input among several, not as a verdict.
Cardholder C08623 reported on 2016-12-10 15:01:21, two hours after the charge: 'I never made this $49.00 purchase. Please check my card.'

Asked whether they were in billing region 330.0 on 2016-12-10 and whether they recognised the $116.93 charge 49 minutes earlier, the cardholder confirmed both: they were in the area and made the larger purchase, but still do not recognise the $49.00 charge.

case.summary: Cardholder C08623 disputes a $49.00 card-present purchase in billing region 330.0. On the graph evidence the charge is unremarkable for this card: the region carries 42 prior transactions going back to July, 53 earlier charges sit in the same dollar band, the amount is below the cardholder's median, and the product and channel are their norm. Against that, this cardholder has denied activity five times before and been correct five times, all on this same card, and a $116.93 charge 49 minutes earlier in the same region scored 0.88. The two signals conflict, so the case was not closed on the graph alone. Verification placed the cardholder in region 330.0 that day and confirmed the larger adjacent charge as theirs, which removed the strongest fraud indicator and dropped assessed probability from 0.55 to 0.32; the cardholder nonetheless maintains the dispute. No block is recommended at any stage: the charge matches the cardholder's own established pattern (R7) and there is no shared device, region cluster or connected card to justify one.

evidence_requests.assumed_response: Cardholder confirms they were in billing region 330.0 on 2016-12-10 and recognises transaction 3530056 ($116.93 at 12:12:41) as their own purchase, but continues to state they did not make the $49.00 charge at 13:01:21. Assumption basis: the card has 42 prior transactions in region 330.0 including four on 2016-12-07 and one on 2016-12-09, so the cardholder demonstrably frequents the area; a small forgotten charge is the most likely explanation consistent with that history.

VERIFY_WITH_CUSTOMER is therefore replaced by WARN_CUSTOMER under R7. No block was recommended at either stage: R1 barred it before the evidence came in, and R7 bars it after.

sar.reason: 3a: no report. Fraud is neither confirmed nor strongly suspected at probability 0.32, exposure of $49.00 is far below the $1,000 threshold, and the activity connects to no shared device profile, no region cluster and no other customer's fraud. Region 330.0 shows 18 of 608 transactions scoring 0.70 or above across the alert window against 13 of 552 a month earlier, which is not a cluster. FILE_REPORT does not appear in the final actions.

stop_reason: Policy 6, second condition: the verification response settled the decisive question. The cardholder confirmed their presence in region 330.0 and ownership of the adjacent higher-risk charge, which is the only piece of evidence that could have turned a statistically ordinary purchase into a fraud episode. Probability now sits at 0.32, outside the 0.15/0.85 band, so the case is escalated rather than closed. No further graph evidence would change the action set, because the remaining question is whether the cardholder simply forgot a $49 purchase, and no query can answer that.
